source_meta._title: "FOV Effects" slider incorrectly modifying zoom values on the spyglass

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w33a, unmodified vanilla client with no mods. Use a single-player Creative-mode world as the simplest deterministic way to obtain a spyglass; the report does not require multiplayer, a dedicated server, a specific seed, coordinates, commands, experiments, or a particular fullscreen/windowed state.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has a playable installation for the exact snapshot version 24w33a.
The client is vanilla and has no mods installed or loaded, matching the report.
A mouse or equivalent input is available for the bound Use Item/Place Block action; its default keyboard-and-mouse binding is right-click.
Use one unchanged player position and one stationary visual target for both spyglass tests so that the two settings are directly comparable.
Do not use fix version 24w34a for the reproduction.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and launch the exact Java Edition installation named or configured for snapshot 24w33a. Use a clean vanilla profile or game directory without mods.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu opens and displays 24w33a as the running version, normally in the lower-left corner.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new world with Game Mode set to Creative, or load an existing disposable Creative-mode world created in 24w33a. No particular seed or experiments are required. Creative mode is an item-acquisition convenience rather than a condition stated by the report.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a 24w33a world and has access to the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Do not begin the test immediately on world entry. Wait until nearby terrain has rendered and looking or moving responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Surrounding chunks are visible and camera movement is responsive without world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control, which is E by default.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and shows category tabs and the player hotbar.

steps.action: Select the Search Items tab and enter the item name "spyglass" in the search field.
steps.exact_input: spyglass
steps.success_cue: A Spyglass item is visible in the Creative inventory search results.

steps.action: Move one Spyglass from the search results into any empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.exact_input: Left-click or shift-click the Spyglass into an empty hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: A Spyglass icon is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E, then select the hotbar slot containing the Spyglass by scrolling to it or pressing its corresponding number key, 1 through 9.
steps.exact_input: E, then the number key corresponding to the Spyglass hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Spyglass is highlighted in the hotbar and is visible in the player's main hand.

steps.action: Choose a stationary, clearly defined visual target, such as the edge of a distant block, tree, building, or terrain feature. If necessary, fly to an open area first. Stand still, center the crosshair on the target, and do not change the player's position between the 100% and 0% tests. A target several blocks away is sufficient; the report's four-block-gap arrangement was a comparison aid rather than a stated prerequisite.
steps.exact_input: Center the crosshair on one stationary target; release all movement controls
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary with the same identifiable target centered or otherwise clearly framed on screen.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Options, select Video Settings, and locate the slider labeled "FOV Effects" as specified by the report. Do not change the separate general FOV setting.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Video Settings -> FOV Effects
steps.success_cue: The FOV Effects slider is visible in the settings interface.

steps.action: Adjust the FOV Effects slider to exactly 100%. Move the slider fully to its maximum if necessary, and confirm that its displayed value reads 100%.
steps.success_cue: The FOV Effects control visibly reads 100%.

steps.action: Select Done as needed until gameplay resumes. Do not press movement controls or relocate the player.
steps.exact_input: Done -> Done
steps.success_cue: The world view is active again, the Spyglass remains selected, and the player remains at the comparison position.

steps.action: Re-center the same target if needed, then press and hold the bound Use Item/Place Block action while the Spyglass is selected. With default keyboard-and-mouse controls, hold the right mouse button. Continue holding until the spyglass viewing overlay is fully visible. The default right-button Use action is externally documented. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ABeginner%27s_guide?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Hold right mouse button (default Use Item/Place Block)
steps.success_cue: The spyglass viewing overlay is fully visible while the Use action remains held.

steps.action: Release the Use Item/Place Block action to stop using the Spyglass. Keep the player at exactly the same position and retain the same target for the lower-setting test.
steps.exact_input: Release right mouse button
steps.success_cue: The spyglass overlay has disappeared, the Spyglass remains selected, and the player has not changed position.

steps.action: Open Esc -> Options -> Video Settings again, locate FOV Effects, and set it to exactly 0%. The report states that any value below 100% can be tested; 0% is selected here as the clearest deterministic lower-than-100% value.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Video Settings -> FOV Effects -> 0%
steps.success_cue: The FOV Effects control visibly reads 0%.

steps.action: Select Done as needed to resume gameplay. Without walking, flying, sprinting, changing the general FOV option, or switching items, aim at the same stationary target used for the 100% test.
steps.exact_input: Done -> Done; release movement controls
steps.success_cue: The Spyglass is selected, the player is at the original comparison position, and the same target is framed on screen.

steps.action: Press and hold the bound Use Item/Place Block action again while aiming at the same target. With default keyboard-and-mouse controls, hold the right mouse button. Keep the input held and hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as the spyglass overlay is fully visible.
steps.exact_input: Hold right mouse button (default Use Item/Place Block)
steps.success_cue: The spyglass viewing overlay is fully visible at FOV Effects 0%, the same target is framed, and the Use action remains held.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just begun using the selected Spyglass while FOV Effects is set to 0%, from the same stationary position and against the same visual target used for the 100% baseline. The spyglass overlay is fully visible and the Use Item/Place Block input remains held; begin observing the camera framing and zoom state now.
uncertainties: The report specifies the navigation path as Video Settings -> FOV Effects, and that path is preserved. External historical material also describes FOV Effects as an accessibility setting, so menu terminology may vary even when referring to the same slider. ([feedback.minecraft.net](https://feedback.minecraft.net/hc/en-us/articles/360057761252-Minecraft-Java-Edition-Snapshot-21w10a?utm_source=openai))
The report does not specify a game mode, seed, coordinates, or server type. Single-player Creative mode is chosen only to obtain the Spyglass quickly and remove unrelated survival setup.

The reporter mentions a four-block-wide gap only as the specific visual comparison used for attached screenshots; its exact construction and orientation are not described. The plan therefore uses one stationary target viewed from one unchanged position rather than inventing unsupported gap geometry.
The report states that fullscreen versus windowed mode does not change the result, so no display-mode requirement is imposed.

source_meta._title: Post shader ColorModulate uniform not reset properly after spectating spiders

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w39a in a clean, unmodded single-player world. Use Creative mode with commands enabled, vanilla resources, no external shader packs, and hardware capable of selecting Fabulous! graphics. The deterministic setup below uses a Superflat world and stationary summoned entities, although the report does not require that world type or summoning method.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to make snapshot versions available and install/select snapshot 24w39a.
Use a clean vanilla installation without mods, external shader packs, or resource packs that alter post-processing or entity visuals.
Ensure the computer's graphics hardware and drivers allow the Graphics option to be set to Fabulous!.
Use the default Attack control (left mouse button) and Sneak control (Left Shift), or identify the equivalent controls if the key bindings have been changed.
Do not use Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.2 Pre-Release 1, because it is listed as a fix version rather than an affected version.
Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1 is mentioned in the report only as an unaffected comparison run; it is not an affected version and is not the target of this reproduction plan.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, enable snapshot installations if necessary, select an installation whose version is exactly snapshot 24w39a, and start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition main menu is open and the displayed version is 24w39a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, select Create New World, and set the game mode to Creative. Ensure commands or cheats are enabled if the world-creation screen exposes a separate command setting.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The new-world configuration shows Creative mode and permits in-game commands.

steps.action: For deterministic visibility and unobstructed entity placement, open the world-type settings and select Superflat. Leave the other world-generation settings at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Superflat
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen identifies the selected world type as Superflat.

steps.action: Create the world. After the loading screen closes, do not continue until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Creative-mode Superflat world and can move normally.

steps.action: Press Esc, open Options, open Video Settings, and activate the Graphics option until its value is Fabulous!. Accept any Fabulous-graphics warning prompt, apply the setting if an Apply button is shown, and return to the world. Allow rendering to stabilize before continuing.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Video Settings -> Graphics: Fabulous!
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world, the Graphics setting is Fabulous!, surrounding terrain is rendered, and controls respond normally.

steps.action: Without moving to a confined location, press T to open in-game chat. Enter the supplied deterministic Enderman summon command, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The NoAI tag keeps the Enderman in place so it remains easy to target.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:enderman ~3 ~ ~ {NoAI:1b}
steps.success_cue: A stationary Enderman appears approximately three blocks along the positive X direction from the player's summon position, and the command reports a successful summon.

steps.action: Remain near the same location. Press T to open chat, enter the deterministic spider summon command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /summon minecraft:spider ~-3 ~ ~ {NoAI:1b}
steps.success_cue: A stationary spider appears approximately three blocks along the negative X direction from the player's summon position, and both the spider and Enderman remain loaded nearby.

steps.action: Press T to open chat, enter the Spectator-mode command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /gamemode spectator
steps.success_cue: The player is in Spectator mode, can fly, and can pass through blocks rather than colliding with them.

steps.action: Turn and, if necessary, fly a short distance until the summoned Enderman is clearly visible. Keep both summoned entities nearby and within loaded chunks.
steps.success_cue: The stationary Enderman is visible at close range and the player remains in free-flying Spectator mode.

steps.action: Aim directly at the Enderman's body so that the center crosshair rests on the entity with no block or other entity between the camera and the Enderman.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the Enderman at a range where it can be selected.

steps.action: Press the Attack control once while targeting the Enderman; with default controls, left-click once. Do not hold the mouse button.
steps.exact_input: Left-click once while the crosshair is on the Enderman
steps.success_cue: The camera is attached to the Enderman's viewpoint rather than moving as a free-flying spectator.

steps.action: Press and release the Sneak control once to stop spectating the Enderman; with default controls, press Left Shift once.
steps.exact_input: Left Shift
steps.success_cue: The camera has detached from the Enderman and the player can once again fly independently in Spectator mode. Fabulous! graphics remains selected.

steps.action: Turn toward the summoned spider and, if necessary, fly a short distance until it is clearly visible. Aim at the spider's body with an unobstructed line of sight.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the stationary spider at a range where it can be selected.

steps.action: Press the Attack control once while targeting the spider; with default controls, left-click once. Do not hold the mouse button.
steps.exact_input: Left-click once while the crosshair is on the spider
steps.success_cue: The camera is attached to the spider's viewpoint rather than moving as a free-flying spectator.

steps.action: Press and release the Sneak control once to stop spectating the spider; with default controls, press Left Shift once. Do not open any menus, change the Graphics option, spectate another entity, or perform another post-processing transition after this input.
steps.exact_input: Left Shift
steps.success_cue: The camera has just detached from the spider, the player is back in free-flying Spectator mode, and Graphics is still set to Fabulous!.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just exited the spider's spectator viewpoint by pressing Sneak and is now a free-flying spectator while Fabulous! graphics remains enabled. No subsequent graphics change or entity-spectating action has occurred. Begin visual observation immediately in this state.
uncertainties: The report does not prescribe a world type. Superflat is selected only as a practical way to provide an open, deterministic testing area.

The report says to spawn an Enderman and a spider but does not prescribe spawn eggs or commands. The plan uses modern summon commands with NoAI tags as a practical deterministic method for snapshot 24w39a; the entities' stationary state is not asserted to be required by the bug.

The report also describes changing to Fast Graphics, spectating the Enderman a second time, and repeating the sequence in Java Edition 1.21.1. Those are post-trigger diagnostic and comparison procedures. They are not included in the primary run because changing graphics immediately after step 15 would alter the first directly observable trigger state before the observation subsystem can inspect it.

source_meta._title: Sprinting isn't canceled when dismounting rideable entities while sprinting

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client running the exact historical snapshot 13w36a. Use a local single-player Creative-mode Superflat world with keyboard and mouse controls. The operational plan assumes the default bindings W for Move Forward, Left Ctrl for Sprint, Left Shift for Sneak/Dismount, E for Inventory, and right-click for Use Item/Interact; if controls are rebound, use the keys currently assigned to those actions. No dedicated server, additional players, commands, cheats, seed, datapack, resource pack, or mod is required.
preconditions: Install or configure a Minecraft Launcher installation for the exact Java Edition snapshot 13w36a; do not use 13w36b, 1.7.2, a fix version, or a modern release for the recommended run.
Use an unmodified client so that mods do not alter movement, riding, camera FOV, or sprint controls.
Confirm under Options -> Controls that Move Forward, Sprint, and Sneak are bound and can be pressed simultaneously. With default controls these are W, Left Ctrl, and Left Shift.
Use the dedicated Sprint action required by the report rather than initiating sprint by double-tapping W.
Keep the player on the ground. Do not enter Creative flight by double-tapping Space.
Use an adult pig. A piglet is not suitable because it cannot be saddled and mounted for this procedure.
Leave at least one hotbar slot empty so the player can mount the pig without holding an item that has another right-click interaction.
Perform the test in a clear area where the pig and player cannot immediately collide with walls, fall from an edge, enter water, or take damage.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher installation configured for the exact snapshot 13w36a and wait for the game to reach its main menu.
steps.exact_input: Launch Minecraft Java Edition 13w36a
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed and the lower-left version label identifies 13w36a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world menu and begin creating a new world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative so the required pig spawn egg and saddle can be obtained without exploration or crafting.
steps.exact_input: Click Game Mode until it reads Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The world configuration screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Configure a flat, unobstructed test world. Open the additional world options, cycle the world type to Superflat, and return to the main world-creation screen. Leave the seed unspecified.
steps.exact_input: More World Options... -> click World Type until Superflat is selected -> Done
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is configured for Creative mode and the Superflat world type.

steps.action: Create the world.
steps.exact_input: Create New World
steps.success_cue: World generation begins.

steps.action: Wait for world loading to finish before setting up the pig. Do not continue while the terrain is blank, still rapidly appearing, or player input is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the Superflat surface, nearby terrain is rendered, the HUD is visible, and looking or walking responds normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and the hotbar is visible at the bottom.

steps.action: Locate a pig spawn egg and a saddle in the Creative inventory. If necessary, hover over candidate items and read their tooltips to distinguish the pig egg from other spawn eggs. Place the pig spawn egg in hotbar slot 1, the saddle in hotbar slot 2, and leave hotbar slot 3 empty.
steps.exact_input: Pig spawn egg -> hotbar slot 1; Saddle -> hotbar slot 2; hotbar slot 3 left empty
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains a pig spawn egg, slot 2 contains a saddle, and slot 3 is empty.

steps.action: Close the inventory and return to first-person world control.
steps.exact_input: E
steps.success_cue: The inventory closes and the crosshair is visible in the world.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1, aim the crosshair at an unobstructed ground block a few blocks away, and use the pig spawn egg. Verify that the spawned pig is full-sized; if a piglet is produced, spawn another pig on an empty ground block and use an adult for the remaining steps.
steps.exact_input: Press 1, then right-click the ground
steps.success_cue: A full-sized adult pig is standing on the flat ground within interaction range.

steps.action: Select the saddle, aim directly at the adult pig, and use the saddle on it once.
steps.exact_input: Press 2, then right-click the adult pig
steps.success_cue: The pig visibly wears a saddle and remains available to mount.

steps.action: Switch to the empty hotbar slot so no held item interferes with interaction. Aim directly at the saddled pig and interact with it to mount.
steps.exact_input: Press 3, then right-click the saddled pig
steps.success_cue: The viewpoint moves onto the pig, the player is seated on it, and the on-screen prompt indicates that the Sneak control can be used to dismount if that prompt is present in this version.

steps.action: While remaining mounted, press and hold Move Forward, then press and continue holding the dedicated Sprint key. Do not initiate sprint by double-tapping forward. Keep both inputs depressed until the next step. The pig does not need to be steered with a carrot on a stick for this state transition.
steps.exact_input: Hold W, then hold Left Ctrl without releasing W
steps.success_cue: The player remains mounted on the saddled pig with both Move Forward and Sprint inputs held; the camera FOV has shifted from its idle view, confirming that the sprint input registered.

steps.action: Without releasing Move Forward or Sprint, press the Sneak/Dismount control once to leave the pig.
steps.exact_input: While still holding W + Left Ctrl, press Left Shift once
steps.success_cue: The player is no longer seated on the pig and is positioned beside or near it; W and Left Ctrl have not yet been released.

steps.action: Immediately release both Move Forward and Sprint, and do not press Sprint again. Allow any short forward movement caused by the held keys to stop, without mounting another entity, opening a menu, attacking, or changing game mode.
steps.exact_input: Release W and Left Ctrl
steps.success_cue: The player is dismounted, no movement or sprint input is being held, ordinary movement has slowed to a stop, and the camera view is unobstructed and ready for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just dismounted the saddled pig while Move Forward and the dedicated Sprint key were held, then released both inputs and slowed to a stop without pressing Sprint again. Begin observing the player's camera/FOV and sprint-state indicators before any further movement or sprint input changes the state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, world type, world seed, single-player versus multiplayer, or server configuration. A local Creative-mode Superflat world is selected only as the simplest deterministic way to obtain and mount a pig.

The report lists 22w44a both as an affected version and as a fix version. It is preserved in affected_versions because the report explicitly lists it there, but it is not selected as the recommended reproduction version.

The historical Creative inventory may label the pig spawn egg as 'Spawn Pig' rather than using modern item-name wording. The executor should identify it by the pig-related tooltip and egg appearance rather than depending on one exact UI label.

The report's later stop-and-restart-sprinting sequence is a post-trigger comparison performed after inspecting the initial state. It is not included beyond the first trigger because this plan hands control to the Observation Agent immediately after the dismount-and-slow-down state is established.

External verification was limited to operational controls and pig interaction details because those details were necessary to turn the report's high-level mounting, sprinting, and dismounting instructions into executable inputs for the historical version.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.4 in single-player on the integrated server, using a fresh Superflat world in Creative mode with cheats enabled. Perform two independent executions of this plan: a lava run using the Lava Bucket and `/tp ~ 62.39 ~`, and a water run using the Water Bucket and `/tp ~ 63.39 ~`. Use a fresh world for each run so that the fluids cannot interact.
preconditions: A launcher installation for the exact historical version Minecraft 1.4.4 is available and can start successfully.

Default movement and interaction controls are assumed: E opens the inventory, T opens chat, Space controls upward movement and toggles Creative flight when double-tapped, left-click breaks a block, and right-click uses or places the selected item.
The test must be performed in Creative mode, and cheats must be enabled so the report's `/tp` command can be executed.
Choose one run before beginning: the lava run or the water run. Complete the setup and hand off for that run, then create another fresh world and repeat for the other fluid.
The player must not have a resource pack, mod, shader, or third-party client installed unless separately required by the reproduction system; none is specified by the report.

Because `/setblock` is unavailable in Minecraft 1.4.4, the source block must be positioned manually with the matching filled bucket. The report's exact source-placement commands are preserved in uncertainties and must not be entered in 1.4.4.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft launcher, select an installation that runs the exact version Minecraft 1.4.4, and launch the game without mods.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 1.4.4
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.4.4 title screen is displayed.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a fresh test world. Set Game Mode to Creative. Open More World Options, set World Type to Superflat, set Allow Cheats to ON, return to the main world-creation screen, and create the world. Do not reuse the same world for the lava and water runs.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> World Type: Superflat -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A fresh Superflat world has loaded and the player is in Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait before building until the terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The nearby Superflat terrain is visible, no loading screen is present, and movement inputs respond immediately.

steps.action: Start Creative flight by quickly pressing the jump control twice. Use Space to rise several blocks and then release all movement controls so the player hovers.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space
steps.success_cue: The player remains suspended in the air instead of falling to the ground.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Put one nonflammable solid building block, such as Stone, in a hotbar slot. For the lava run, also put a Lava Bucket in another hotbar slot. For the water run, instead put a Water Bucket in another hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.exact_input: E; obtain Stone and either Lava Bucket or Water Bucket
steps.success_cue: Stone and exactly the filled bucket selected for this run are visible in separate hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Press F3 to display debug information and choose an integer horizontal target column near the player, denoted (T_x, T_z). The fluid source will occupy block coordinates (T_x, 64, T_z). Ensure this location and the immediately surrounding blocks at Y=64 are open air. Record T_x and T_z for use during alignment.
steps.exact_input: E, then F3
steps.success_cue: The debug overlay is visible, T_x and T_z have been recorded, and the intended block at (T_x, 64, T_z) is open air.

steps.action: Using Stone, construct a temporary one-block-wide support pillar in the adjacent column (T_x+1, T_z). Build upward from the Superflat ground until the top Stone block occupies Y=64. Use Creative flight and the F3 coordinates to control the height; do not place a solid block in the target fluid column (T_x, T_z).
steps.exact_input: Select Stone; right-click repeatedly to place the temporary pillar
steps.success_cue: A Stone support block occupies (T_x+1, 64, T_z), while (T_x, 64, T_z) remains open air.

steps.action: Select the filled bucket in the hotbar by pressing its hotbar number or scrolling to it. Confirm that the bucket name corresponds to the chosen run.
steps.exact_input: Select Lava Bucket for the lava run, or Water Bucket for the water run
steps.success_cue: The matching filled bucket is held in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim at the side face of the Y=64 support block that borders the target air block (T_x, 64, T_z). Right-click once with the filled bucket to place one source block in the target column. Do not place the fluid on top of the support block.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once with the selected filled bucket
steps.success_cue: The selected fluid occupies block (T_x, 64, T_z).

steps.action: Switch to an empty hand or another item. In Creative mode, left-click the temporary support blocks at (T_x+1, 64, T_z), (T_x+1, 63, T_z), and (T_x+1, 62, T_z) to remove them. Do not left-click the fluid source block.
steps.exact_input: Left-click each of the three specified support blocks once
steps.success_cue: No solid support block remains beside the fluid at Y=62 through Y=64, and the source fluid is still present at (T_x, 64, T_z).

steps.action: Wait briefly for fluid and block updates to process. Remain in flight and do not enter the source yet.
steps.success_cue: The source block remains in the target column, nearby fluid movement has updated, and player controls remain responsive.

steps.action: While flying above Y=65, move horizontally over the source. Use the F3 coordinates to place the player's X coordinate within T_x through T_x+1 and Z coordinate within T_z through T_z+1, preferably near the center of the source column. Release all horizontal movement controls once aligned.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed; release all movement keys after alignment
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering above the source with both horizontal coordinates inside the source block's column.

steps.action: Open chat by pressing T. For the lava run, enter the report's exact teleport command `/tp ~ 62.39 ~`. For the water run, enter the report's exact teleport command `/tp ~ 63.39 ~`. Include the leading slash and press Enter once. Do not add a player selector or alter the decimal value.
steps.exact_input:
Lava run: /tp ~ 62.39 ~
Water run: /tp ~ 63.39 ~
steps.success_cue: The command closes chat and moves the player vertically while preserving the aligned X and Z position.

steps.action: If the debug overlay is not already visible, press F3. Confirm that the displayed player Y position is approximately 62.39 for the lava run or 63.39 for the water run, and confirm that X and Z are still inside the chosen source column. Then press F3 again to hide the overlay so it does not obstruct rendering observation.
steps.exact_input: F3 to verify, then F3 to hide
steps.success_cue: The required decimal Y position has been confirmed, the player remains horizontally aligned with the fluid source, and the debug overlay is hidden.

steps.action: Release every movement, jump, and descend control. Do not change altitude or move horizontally during the camera test.
steps.exact_input: Release W, A, S, D, Space, and Left Shift
steps.success_cue: The player remains stationary at the teleported position inside the selected fluid setup.

steps.action: Begin changing only the camera pitch: slowly move the mouse upward until looking steeply upward, then reverse and move it downward until looking steeply downward. Continue a slow up-and-down pitch sweep without moving the player or changing the horizontal viewing direction more than necessary.
steps.exact_input: Slow vertical mouse movement: look up, then look down
steps.success_cue: The camera pitch is actively sweeping up and down while the player's position and altitude remain unchanged.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is stationary at the report-specified Y position, horizontally aligned with the manually placed Y=64 source block, the debug overlay is hidden, and the first slow up-and-down camera sweep has begun. Hand control to the observation subsystem during this sweep; after that run is complete, repeat the plan in a fresh world for the other fluid variant.
uncertainties: The report lists Minecraft 1.4.4 first, so it is the required recommended version. However, the supplied `/setblock` command did not exist in that version; external version history indicates `/setblock` was introduced in snapshot 13w37a for Java Edition 1.7.2. The plan therefore substitutes manual bucket placement only for the unavailable source-placement operation.

The raw report's exact source-placement commands are `/setblock ~ 64 ~ lava` and `/setblock ~ 64 ~ water`. They are intentionally not executed in Minecraft 1.4.4 because they would be unrecognized. If a separate command-exact reproduction is requested, Minecraft 1.7.4 is the first formally listed affected version in this report that postdates the addition of `/setblock`; that does not change the required recommended_version.

Manual bucket placement causes normal fluid updates around the source and may not be perfectly identical to placement by `/setblock`. The source block itself is positioned at the same Y=64 block coordinate required by the report, and nearby temporary solid blocks are removed before triggering the test.

The report supplies no world seed, absolute X/Z coordinates, terrain requirement, or required world type. A fresh Superflat world and an arbitrary recorded target column are practical choices intended to remove terrain and exploration variability.

The report does not specify the exact camera pitch or mouse speed at which the relevant rendering state becomes inspectable. The plan uses a slow sweep across the available upward and downward pitch range while keeping player position fixed.
The lava and water procedures have different teleport heights and are treated as independent runs. Combining them in one location could create stone or cobblestone and invalidate the setup.

source_meta._title: You can retain entities' shaders by running the "/kill" command while in spectator mode

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 14w05a in a disposable singleplayer world using the integrated server. Use a non-Hardcore Creative world with commands enabled for setup, then enter Spectator mode for the trigger. A Superflat world and Normal difficulty are practical choices that keep the Creeper easy to locate and prevent it from disappearing because of Peaceful difficulty. Do not use external shader mods or shader packs.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot Minecraft 14w05a; do not substitute the listed fix snapshot Minecraft 14w05b.
Use a new or otherwise disposable non-Hardcore singleplayer world so that the player can respawn after executing /kill.
Commands must be enabled. When creating the world, select Creative mode and ensure Allow Cheats is ON.
Set difficulty to Easy, Normal, or Hard rather than Peaceful so the summoned Creeper remains present.
Use first-person perspective before beginning the command sequence.
Know the current bindings for Open Chat, Attack/Destroy, and movement. Their defaults are T, left-click, and W/A/S/D.

After entering the Creeper's viewpoint, do not press the dismount control, F4, or any perspective/game-mode shortcut before executing /kill. Those actions may detach the camera or toggle the entity shader.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact historical snapshot Minecraft 14w05a, launch it, and wait for its main menu to appear.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 14w05a
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the main menu running snapshot 14w05a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new disposable world. Select Creative as the game mode, ensure Hardcore is not selected, open More World Options, turn Allow Cheats ON, and optionally select Superflat to make the Creeper easy to locate. Create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The world-loading screen begins and the selected world is non-Hardcore with commands available.

steps.action: Wait until the world has fully loaded. If the difficulty is Peaceful, press Esc, open Options, click the Difficulty button until it displays Normal, select Done, and return to the game. Do not continue until surrounding terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Difficulty: Normal -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a loaded area, and the difficulty is Normal rather than Peaceful.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the historical 14w05a summon command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command places a Creeper three blocks away along the positive Z axis.
steps.exact_input: /summon Creeper ~ ~ ~3
steps.success_cue: A Creeper has been created close to the player; turn around if necessary until it is visible.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, move or turn as needed so that the Creeper is clearly visible and close enough to target with the crosshair. Keep several blocks of open space around it and do not attack it.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D and mouse movement
steps.success_cue: The Creeper is alive, visible, and can be placed under the center crosshair.

steps.action: Press T to open chat, enter the version-compatible numeric Spectator-mode command exactly as shown, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /gamemode 3
steps.success_cue: The player is in Spectator mode, can fly through blocks, and can move without interacting normally with blocks or entities.

steps.action: Approach the Creeper in Spectator mode, center the crosshair directly on its body, and press the Attack/Destroy control once—left-click by default—to begin viewing through the Creeper. Do not use right-click.
steps.exact_input: Left-click (Attack/Destroy) once while the crosshair targets the Creeper
steps.success_cue: The camera is locked to the Creeper's position and orientation, independent player movement no longer moves the camera away from it, and the normal Creeper-view green pixelated post-processing shader is active.

steps.action: Without dismounting from the Creeper, changing game mode, toggling perspective, or pressing F4, press T to open chat. Enter the report's command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Because no target argument is supplied, the command acts on the player executing it.
steps.exact_input: /kill
steps.success_cue: The player dies and the death screen containing the Respawn button is displayed.

steps.action: On the death screen, click the Respawn button once. Do not use Return to Title Screen.
steps.exact_input: Respawn
steps.success_cue: The death screen closes and the world respawn/loading process begins.

steps.action: Wait until the respawn completes, surrounding chunks and entities have rendered, and movement or camera input responds normally. Make no further perspective, shader, or game-mode changes before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world after respawning, terrain is visible, and controls respond normally.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has executed /kill while still attached to the Creeper's Spectator-mode viewpoint, clicked Respawn, and completed world loading without making any additional perspective, shader, or game-mode changes. Begin observation of the respawned surroundings now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, world type, difficulty, or dedicated-server requirement. This plan uses a new singleplayer Superflat Creative world at Normal difficulty as a deterministic setup convenience, not as a claimed bug requirement.

The report says to summon a Creeper but does not supply an exact summon command. The plan uses the historical command /summon Creeper ~ ~ ~3, preserving the pre-1.13 entity-name style appropriate to snapshot 14w05a.

The report does not state which method should be used to enter Spectator mode. The numeric command /gamemode 3 was selected because Spectator mode and the numeric value 3 were available in the recommended snapshot.
The report does not state whether controls are rebound. Instructions name both the gameplay action and its default keyboard or mouse input.
